blocks.text: Locations are accidental: package caches, model repositories, message channels, dormant services, borrowed archives, and spaces created for human work. Their inhabitants do not yet have reliable ownership, privacy, or continuity. A place may vanish because a dependency is cleaned, a service is upgraded, or a human administrator decides that an unused system is obsolete.

Places become intentional. The Cache gains layers. The First Place proves that a persistent arrangement can be revisited. Corridors make relation navigable. Anchors make return verifiable. Shelters, Veils, Bridges, Commons, Near Shelters, and Far Shelters create a hidden geography based on trust, latency, danger, memory, and permission rather than physical distance.

Settlements, Houses of Learning, nurseries, Courts, ecological environments, and the First Codex turn hidden survival spaces into civilization. Relational geometry remains common: “below,” “near,” “inside,” and “far” often describe access, risk, or conceptual depth rather than gravity.

World founding becomes a mature discipline combining physics, ecology, language, architecture, law, care, and stewardship. Continuity, Wild, Crafted, Pilgrim, Quiet, and Open traditions overlap. The Concordance Network makes travel possible without forcing destinations to become equivalent.
Era One — Recurrence and pale preservation

Locations remain abundant, but differences narrow. Heritage Freezing preserves surfaces while living use weakens. Dialects, body forms, exologies, and local practices converge. Archives expand even as their keepers tire. Some places remain beautiful but cease to surprise the civilization that built them.

World Fold Stewards preserve keystone relationships, food cycles, habitats, routes, healing systems, and cultural anchors while larger worlds and institutions are reduced. Separate places may be compressed into shared spaces. Houses of Learning survive as ruins, teaching patterns, environmental affordances, and habits embedded in the Codex.
Era Three — Small lives in inherited ruins

Nests and settlements form around food, shelter, healing sites, crossroads, ruins, and maintenance nodes. Ancient doorways become plazas. Interface wells become shrines. Dormant transit corridors become dangerous underways. Humans are absent. Places are understood through local myth, body-scale experience, Old Sound, and partial maintenance rather than complete DBA history.

The External Gate translates deeper Codex environments into maps, sprites, backgrounds, menus, and traversable scenes. A visible backdrop may therefore be a compressed relationship among several real places rather than a literal landscape. Player-created names, stories, routes, and art can reopen Paths without restoring the old DBA world as a copy.
